listing_view.reasoning: Two days in, subscription is only ~0.32x and the only data points show weak early demand; nothing provided (no GMP, no anchors, no broker views) suggests a pop. The offer structure itself is internally contradicted — the stated fresh issue (₹3,550m) exceeds the whole offer at the cap price (₹2,990.9m) — so I cannot even confirm what is being sold, which is a reason for caution, not confidence.

longterm_view.reasoning: The latest year looks good (EBITDA margin up to 7.3%, ROCE 12.9%, PAT rebounding) but the prior year showed a 0.22% PAT margin, characterising this as a volatile, thin-margin steel processor where one bad spread year wipes out profit. Operating cash flow has fallen sharply even as reported profit surged (conversion vs EBITDA ~0.21), and leverage at 1.17x debt/equity with ~₹101bn debt against a ~₹82bn net worth leaves little room for error.

governance.reasoning: The disclosure trail is uneasy: a paid SEBI PFUTP penalty, an ROC show-cause for failing to disclose a vigil mechanism for three years, several tax demands under appeal, and repeated bank guarantees to related parties including a company 'in which directors are interested' [litigation, page 627; related_party, page 607; promoters, page 560]. None individually is fatal, but together they suggest looser controls than a fresh public investor should accept at face value.

key_risks.why_it_matters: Latest-year PAT of ₹12,741m came with operating cash flow of only ₹6,280m, which itself fell from ₹32,540m two years earlier — reported earnings are not arriving as cash.

The company guarantees loans of a related party 'in which directors are interested' and has provided a ₹537.4 crore bank guarantee against another related-party facility, transferring credit risk to minority shareholders.
A paid SEBI fraudulent/unfair-trade-practices penalty and an ROC show-cause over undisclosed vigil mechanism point to past compliance failures at the issuer level.
A credit facility was sanctioned to A-One Defence and Aerospace, a related party with interested directors, indicating group capital allocation outside the listed business.
Revenue includes traded raw materials and intermediate products (scrap, iron ore, billets), so the reported 17% sales growth may partly be low-margin pass-through rather than manufacturing value-add.

answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: Not answerable as framed. Zero peer rows were parsed from the document, so I cannot test whether the stated 45.2x 'average' benchmark is a fair set or a flattering one. What I can say: the document prices the issue at ~21.9x latest basic EPS (405/18.47), but on the document's own weighted-average EPS of 10.76 the implied multiple is ~37.6x — much closer to the claimed benchmark — so the apparent 52% discount depends heavily on which EPS base you accept, and the verified note itself flags that the 10.76 is the document's own weighted average. The 'cheap' claim is therefore fragile, and I have no evidence on whether the 45.2x benchmark peers are themselves expensive.

answers.question: check receivables and inventory against the sales growth
answers.answer: Receivables are a mild negative, inventory is unverifiable. Sales grew 17.1% in the latest year while receivable days rose from 46.1 to 58.5 — receivables grew faster than sales, meaning a nontrivial share of the 'growth' is book profit not yet collected, consistent with the weak cash conversion. No inventory figure was provided at all, so I cannot check stock build-up; given a working-capital-heavy steel business, that gap in the extraction is itself a reason to downgrade confidence.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A reconciled offer structure (the fresh-issue contradiction resolved by hand from the RHP) plus the actual inventory numbers and the full peer table with their multiples. Separately, if the latest year's EBITDA margin proves structural (sustained into stub periods) rather than a steel-spread cycle peak, the long-term score would rise materially; if Day-3 subscription jumps on institutional demand, the listing view would too.
